PullRequest.Title: markdown: Update markdown editor to 0.0.2-113
PullRequest.Body: Bumps `@vscode/markdown-editor` from `0.0.2-107` to `0.0.2-113` and updates the lockfile. **Copy button** See top-left of the markdown editor in the codeblock. Now a _Copy_ button appears! **Validation** - `npm ci --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org --no-audit --no-fund` — passed. - `npm run compile` (via `./scripts/code.sh`) — passed; manually checked in Code OSS. - `npm --prefix extensions/markdown-language-features run test-markdown-editor-package-json` — 8 tests passed. - Markdown editor build, manifest consistency check, and targeted type check — passed. *🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a Markdown file in the experimental custom Markdown editor, including documents with many fenced code blocks.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The extension creates one webview for the editor, embeds the document's initial text, and loads the esbuild-produced markdown-editor bundle; the package parses and renders before posting the existing ready message. The diff only selects a newer package build and does not add a host-side stage to this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the bundled markdown-editor JavaScript/CSS/assets from the extension's markdown-editor-out resources into the webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bundle graph per created webview, with normal webview/browser resource caching on warm loads; document code-block count does not multiply host filesystem reads for the package bundle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Version 0.0.2-107 was bundled and loaded through the same resource path once per webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold resource loading is required before the custom editor can render; warm resources may be cached. The dependency version changes bytes but not the number or placement of loads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exchange webview ready/update messages and optional code-block-provider descriptors between the webview and extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A constant ready message per webview, an optional authoritative update, and provider messages grouped by registered provider; no added per-code-block host message is visible in the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same webview handshake and full-document synchronization existed with version 0.0.2-107.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The ready handshake gates synchronization after the initial render, but its cardinality and payload shape are unchanged by the manifest-only version bump.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read static contributed embedded-code-editor HTML resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one read per registered static provider when an editor is initialized or provider caches are explicitly refreshed, independent of fenced-code-block count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider loop and read cardinality applied before the dependency update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provider loading starts during editor resolution and may affect when provider descriptors become available, but rendering can initialize independently; the package bump does not add or increase these reads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Document bytes and rendered block count drive the package's existing parse/DOM work; effective host-boundary cardinality remains one webview and grouped provider operations, not one filesystem or IPC request per code block.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One initialization flow per opened webview. Static provider reads remain sequential in the existing provider loop; dynamic provider resolutions retain existing promise caches. No new burst or limiter change is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The bundle uses normal webview resource caching; provider APIs and resolved code-block editors remain coalesced in existing maps. The lockfile shows the same transitive dependency set, and the diff does not alter cache keys, invalidation, negative-cache behavior, or lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that host-side critical-path boundaries, cardinality, cache lifecycle, and concurrency are unchanged; low confidence in any hypothetical internal package micro-cost, so none is reported.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The private package's internal source delta is not included in the repository diff, so exact DOM/allocation changes inside 0.0.2-113 cannot be quantified. The visible lockfile shows no transitive dependency additions, and there is no changed evidence of a scaling or blocking mechanism sufficient for a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the changed lines only update the package artifact and integrity, with no concrete evidence that the new version adds scaling eager work, synchronous layout, retention, or boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit or interact with code blocks in an already-open Markdown custom editor.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: User edits update the package model and use the existing webview-to-extension edit message, serialized edit queue, and workspace.applyEdit path. Code-block UI interactions are handled in the bundled editor; the manifest change does not alter the host edit protocol or place a new host operation on every keystroke or render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send incremental edit messages from the webview and apply them through the extension host/workspace edit API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized host edit operation per emitted model edit; document-change echoes are suppressed by the existing expected-content check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Version 0.0.2-107 used the same integration entrypoint and host edit queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This path gates persistence of user edits, but the package version line does not change the protocol, queue, or host-side call count.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write selected code text to the platform clipboard when the newly advertised copy control is invoked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one clipboard operation per explicit user activation; no repository diff evidence shows polling, per-render clipboard access, or fan-out by block count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior package version did not advertise this code-block copy interaction in the PR context; there is no evidence that its addition performs expensive work before invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The operation is user-triggered and off the typing/render critical path until invoked.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Interactive cost scales with emitted edits or explicit copy activations, while the unchanged host queue serializes workspace edits. A document may contain many code blocks, but the diff provides no evidence of per-block host IPC, filesystem work, or retained external resources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workspace edits remain serialized by RecoveringTaskQueue. Clipboard interaction is explicit and singular; no changed aggregate concurrency burst is established.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing webview model and provider caches remain in force; this update changes no host cache lookup, invalidation, coalescing, or negative-cache handling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that host IPC and workspace-edit behavior are unchanged; insufficient evidence for a concrete package-internal regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Internal rendering details of the package build are unavailable in the supplied patch. A copy control may add small DOM state per rendered code block, but neither the allocation size nor a user-visible performance consequence is evidenced strongly enough to report.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the visible feature is user-triggered, and the diff does not establish repeated expensive work, blocked input, unbounded retention, or boundary fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file manifest/lockfile diff and traced custom-editor startup, rendering, code-block interaction, host IPC, filesystem/provider reads, cache behavior, and concurrency. The package's transitive dependency set and all repository-visible boundary cardinalities are unchanged. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or proven regression fix was found.
